core_obligations: Produce the deformation functor (proof lines 5946-5952): localize the functor Aut(x) at the identity of x_0 to obtain the predeformation functor F; by the (RS) permanence lemmas it is a deformation functor, and its tangent space F(k[epsilon]) carries the natural k-vector space structure.

Identify addition with composition (proof lines 5954-5976): define addition by pushing forward along the inverse of the (RS) bijection to F(k[epsilon] x_k k[epsilon]) and then along the ring map sending both generators to epsilon; since the transition maps are group homomorphisms for composition and the unit behaves as a zero, addition is a group homomorphism whose neutral behaviour forces it to coincide with composition, so composition in the tangent space is commutative.

Identify the two tangent spaces (proof lines 5978-5988): unwinding the definitions, the tangent space of Aut(x) consists of the automorphisms of the pushforward of x to k[epsilon] which are trivial modulo epsilon, while that of Aut(x_0) consists of the corresponding automorphisms of the pushforward of x_0, and since x_0 is the pushforward of x to k the two sets agree canonically, giving an isomorphism of k-vector spaces.
proof_roadmap: Localize the automorphism functor to obtain a deformation functor and put the standard vector space structure on its tangent space.
Define addition through the (RS) product decomposition and show that it is composition by a group-theoretic argument.
Compare the tangent spaces of the automorphism functors of x and x_0 by unwinding the localization.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a category cofibred in groupoids satisfying (RS) and an object x over A with pushforward x_0, the tangent space of the automorphism group of x is a k-vector space whose addition is composition, and that it is canonically isomorphic to the tangent space of the automorphism group of x_0 (statement lines 5928-5944). The proof (proof lines 5946-5998) localizes the automorphism functor to a deformation functor, defines addition via the (RS) decomposition and identifies it with composition by a group-theoretic argument, and compares the two tangent spaces by unwinding definitions. H3: an original identification of two structures through an explicit group-theoretic argument, written out in full.
